candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
candidate.educational_objective: State the federal documentation and authentication requirement for verbal/telephone orders.

options.A: The order may remain unsigned if the nurse performs read-back.
options.B: The order must be dated, timed, and promptly authenticated by the ordering practitioner or another practitioner responsible for the client’s care when permitted by state law and hospital policy.
options.C: Telephone orders do not become part of the medical record.
options.D: Only the nurse’s initials are required; practitioner authentication is unnecessary.

candidate.rationale: Under 42 CFR §482.24(c)(2), all orders, including verbal orders, must be dated, timed, and authenticated promptly by the ordering practitioner or another practitioner responsible for the client’s care when authorized under state law, hospital policy, and medical staff rules.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Verbal/telephone orders require date, time, and prompt practitioner authentication under applicable law and hospital policy.
candidate.source_document_title: 42 CFR § 482.24(c)(2), Condition of Participation: Medical record services
candidate.source_locator: §482.24(c)(2)—all orders, including verbal orders, must be dated, timed, and authenticated promptly
candidate.stem: A nurse receives a telephone medication order from an authorized practitioner. Which documentation requirement applies under the federal hospital Conditions of Participation?
